items.title: Quantum algorithms for multidimensional partial differential equations
items.subtitle: Quantum linear-algebra methods for scientific PDE workloads
items.summary: Research on quantum methods for solving multidimensional PDEs, including circuit-efficient formulations, practical case studies, and singular-value-based approaches.
overview: This research explores how quantum linear-algebra techniques can be used to formulate and solve multidimensional partial differential equations that arise across scientific and engineering applications.
The work emphasizes practical circuit structure, scalability, and validation across representative PDE families rather than treating the quantum algorithm as an isolated mathematical primitive.

sections.heading: Research direction
paragraphs: The central question is how to map structured PDE problems into quantum computations while keeping the circuit construction efficient enough to study on simulators and available hardware.
Recent work extends this direction toward singular-value decomposition and transformation methods for PDEs in areas such as computational fluid dynamics and nuclear physics.

items.title: Collaborative and Heuristic Particle Track Reconstruction
items.subtitle: Collaborative reconstruction, search algorithms, and reproducible performance studies for high-energy physics
items.summary: Research on particle track building using helical EKF reconstruction, collaborative candidate sharing, metaheuristic search, and reproducible mkFit benchmarking.
items.visualAlt: Optimization progress plot produced by the Particle-Track-Building project, showing reconstruction objective and runtime across trials.
items.visualCaption: Optimizer progress output from the particle track reconstruction work.
overview: This research treats particle track reconstruction as both an estimation problem and a search problem. A helical extended Kalman filter provides the reconstruction core while multiple candidate-building strategies explore how to improve quality, throughput, and robustness.

A major direction is collaborative reconstruction: parallel track candidates share information and coordinate hit usage rather than behaving as completely independent searches. The work also studies heuristic and metaheuristic algorithms and uses mkFit benchmarking infrastructure to evaluate performance and reproducibility.

sections.heading: Reconstruction and search methods
items: Ant colony and particle swarm optimization

sections.heading: Collaborative reconstruction
paragraphs: The collaborative methods investigate how parallel reconstruction workers can share candidate quality information, coordinate hit ownership, and prune weaker hypotheses while preserving reconstruction quality.

sections.heading: Performance and reproducibility
paragraphs: The mkbench tooling provides a Docker-first workflow for building and comparing mkFit variants, running controlled scaling studies, preserving geometry and run configuration, and producing machine-readable performance reports.
items: Throughput, latency, CPU, and memory measurements

sections.heading: Research objective
paragraphs: The broader objective is to understand which collaborative, heuristic, and high-performance strategies make track building more efficient without sacrificing reconstruction quality.
